angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 598,302 km at 177.20 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6435 +/- 0.0189 mas (same row, RUWE 1.36): 177.20 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.86 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Santerne et al. 2016, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-29 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract): 598,302 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.94 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Santerne et al. 2016, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-29 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5358 +/- 38 K from Santerne et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-29 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Santerne et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-29 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-29.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.542, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-29 (pscomppars): spectral type G7 V, from Santerne et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, WASP-152: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-29 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.16 dex, from Santerne et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-29 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.29533, from Barros et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016A&A...594A.100B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-29 (pscomppars): age 2.6 Gyr, from Santerne et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-29 (pscomppars): rotation period 10.79 d, from Santerne et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract)

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/705/A142/tablea1 (Physical properties study of planet systems), column Prot: 10.76 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place
VizieR J/ApJS/276/44/table1 (TIC star magnetic activity with LAMOST DR10 MRS sp.), column Prot: 6.06317 d, the row 0.5 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-29 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3.7 km/s, from Santerne et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016ApJ...824...55S/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.86 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.918. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the K2 mission's own light curve of campaign 4 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43): 10.68 d, the light swinging by 1.5% as the star turns (the light repeats every 5.34 d, half the catalogued rotation period, and the star is taken to turn once in two of them)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
